topic: Medicine and first-aid basics for a 72-hour plan

content.hook: POV: it's 9 pm and the pharmacy is closed

slides.title: POV: 9 pm and the *pharmacy* is closed
slides.body: Medicine and first-aid basics for your 72-hour plan.

slides.title: List every *regular medicine*
slides.body: One line per person: name, and what it's for. Ask your pharmacist about a small spare buffer.

slides.title: Build a simple *first-aid kit*
slides.body: Plasters, bandages, sterile dressings, gloves, scissors, thermometer. One box, one known place.

slides.title: Put it on *paper*
slides.body: Allergies, medicines, doctor's number. Phones die. A sheet in the kit does not.

slides.title: Check it *twice a year*
slides.body: Check expiry dates. Store cool, dry, away from children. Pack a small health pouch for your go-bag.

slides.title: Calm plan. *Ready* before you need it.

content.caption:
First-aid kit and medicine checklist for your 72-hour plan. Picture it: it's 9 pm, the pharmacy is closed and someone at home needs their medicine. These basics are a quiet but important part of any household preparedness plan.

Four calm steps:
1. List everyone's regular medicines. Ask your pharmacist about a small spare buffer.
2. Keep a simple first-aid kit in one known place.
3. Write allergies and doctor contacts on paper, in case phones are down.
4. Check expiry dates twice a year.

This is general guidance in line with civil-protection agencies like MSB, BBK and RCB. It's not medical advice, so talk to your doctor or pharmacist about your own needs.
